title: Rigid body mechanics
summary: Torque, rotational equilibrium, angular kinematics, moment of inertia, Newton’s second law for rotation, angular momentum and rotational kinetic energy.

keyterms.definition: Turning effect of a force about an axis: τ = Fr sin θ, measured in N m.
Two equal, opposite, non-collinear forces giving a resultant torque but no resultant force.
The state in which the resultant torque on a body is zero, so its angular velocity is constant.
Rate of change of angular velocity, α = Δω/Δt, in rad s⁻².
Resistance of a body to angular acceleration, I = Σmr²; depends on mass distribution about the axis.
L = Iω; conserved when no resultant external torque acts.
Kinetic energy of a rotating body, E_k = ½Iω² = L²/2I.
Change in angular momentum produced by a torque, ΔL = τΔt.
Motion where the contact point is momentarily at rest, so v = ωr for the centre of mass.

questions.prompt: A 20 N force acts at the end of a 0.30 m spanner, at 90° to it. What torque does it produce?

questions.statement: A body in rotational equilibrium must be at rest.
questions.explanation: Zero resultant torque means constant angular velocity, which may be non-zero.

questions.text: A force applied along a line passing through the pivot produces a torque of ___.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular distance (sin θ with θ = 0) is zero, so τ = 0.

questions.prompt: A couple acting on a body produces
options: a resultant force but no torque
a torque but no resultant force
questions.explanation: The two forces cancel, so there is no translational acceleration, only rotation.

questions.prompt: A wheel accelerates uniformly from rest to 12 rad s⁻¹ in 4.0 s. Through what angle does it turn?

questions.text: The angular acceleration in the previous wheel example is ___ rad s⁻².
questions.explanation: α = Δω/Δt = 12/4.0 = 3.0 rad s⁻².

questions.prompt: Match each linear quantity to its rotational analogue.
questions.explanation: Rotational equations mirror linear ones with these substitutions.

questions.statement: For a body rolling without slipping, the speed of its centre equals ωr.
questions.explanation: The contact point is instantaneously at rest, so the centre moves at ωr relative to the ground.

questions.prompt: A uniform 4.0 m plank of weight 200 N is supported at its centre. A 300 N child sits 1.0 m from the centre. How far on the other side must a 150 N child sit for balance?
questions.explanation: Moments about the centre: 300 × 1.0 = 150 × d, so d = 2.0 m. The plank’s weight acts at the pivot.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to solve a static equilibrium problem for an extended body.
items: Draw all forces at their points of application
Choose a pivot that eliminates an unknown force
Set clockwise moments equal to anticlockwise moments
Use resultant force = 0 to find remaining forces
questions.explanation: Taking moments about the point where an unknown force acts removes it from the torque equation.

lessons.title: Moment of inertia and angular momentum

questions.prompt: Two wheels have equal mass and radius. Wheel X has its mass concentrated at the rim; wheel Y is a uniform disc. Which has the larger moment of inertia?
options: It depends on the angular velocity
questions.explanation: I = Σmr²: mass further from the axis contributes more, so the rim-loaded wheel has the larger I.

questions.text: A net torque of 6.0 N m acts on a flywheel of moment of inertia 2.0 kg m². Its angular acceleration is ___ rad s⁻².
questions.explanation: τ = Iα, so α = 6.0/2.0 = 3.0 rad s⁻².

questions.prompt: A spinning skater pulls her arms in. Which statement is correct?
options: Her angular velocity increases and angular momentum is unchanged
Her rotational kinetic energy is unchanged
questions.explanation: With no external torque L = Iω is conserved; I falls so ω rises. E_k = L²/2I increases, supplied by the work her muscles do.

questions.statement: Rotational kinetic energy is conserved whenever angular momentum is conserved.
questions.explanation: L can be conserved while E_k changes, as when a skater pulls in her arms and does internal work.

questions.text: A flywheel with I = 0.50 kg m² spins at 20 rad s⁻¹. Its rotational kinetic energy is ___ J.

questions.prompt: A disc with I = 0.40 kg m² spins at 10 rad s⁻¹. A ring of I = 0.10 kg m², initially not rotating, is dropped onto it and they spin together. What is the final angular velocity?
questions.explanation: L conserved: 0.40 × 10 = 0.50 × ω, so ω = 8.0 rad s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: Match each equation to what it describes.
questions.explanation: These are the rotational counterparts of F = ma, p = mv, ½mv² and FΔt.

questions.prompt: A solid ball and a hollow ball of the same mass and radius roll without slipping down the same slope from rest. Which reaches the bottom first?
questions.explanation: The solid ball has the smaller I, so a smaller fraction of its energy becomes rotational KE and more becomes translational KE.

questions.statement: A torque of 4.0 N m acting for 3.0 s changes the angular momentum of a body by 12 kg m² s⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Angular impulse ΔL = τΔt = 4.0 × 3.0 = 12 kg m² s⁻¹ (equivalently N m s).

questions.prompt: Why does a long pole help a tightrope walker keep balance?
options: It increases her moment of inertia, so a given torque produces a smaller angular acceleration
questions.explanation: α = τ/I; a large I slows any tipping, giving time to correct it.
